programme.title: Larry Session Governor and Context-Rotation Layer

phase.summary: Phase 1 (Opus architecture) is complete and settled. Phase 2 is implementing the seven components against it. T-01, T-02, T-07, T-09, T-03, T-13 and T-10 resolved earlier; this banking adds T-11, which CLOSES THE ROTATION LOOP and turns the canonical location into an enforced control. A cleared session now reorients itself automatically from banked state (pointer brief, hard 10,000-char cap), verifies its actual cwd, repository root, branch and HEAD against that state before any implementation, and is refused Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and mutating Bash by a committed PreToolUse gate whenever it is in the wrong place - absolute-path luck is explicitly not a control. Both hooks are activated by a committed idempotent installer, which also reconciled the long-dangling ensure-watcher SessionStart hook. T-14 (build-session registry/launcher by name, automatic programme PR, exact-head QA binding, single merge decision) is now THE next action; T-04 (evaluator) remains independently takable.

tickets.title: Pure evaluator: evaluate(signals) to verdict
tickets.note: 34/34 ticket tests, including a full 64-combination power-set sweep over the 6-signal vocabulary (contextUsedPercentage, rateLimitFiveHourUsedPercentage, growthProjectedRedBeforeCompletion, compactions, bankedStateStale, safeBoundary) asserting the verdict shape stays valid and BLIND fires iff contextUsedPercentage is absent, for every combination. 420/420 suite-wide, no regressions. AD-11 purity: zero filesystem/git/myPKA imports (evaluate(signals) takes a plain object only). Priority BLIND > RECOVERY > RED > AMBER > GREEN, five distinct exit codes (0-4). Missing-field semantics: only contextUsedPercentage is required; every other absent signal is unknown, skipped, and never escalates to BLIND on its own. Judgement call recorded: section 4's states table defines RECOVERY as authoritative-state-already-lost and places it OFF the main axis, while the adjacent threshold bullets describe compaction count as an AMBER/RED FLOOR on that axis -- the two do not fully agree. This implementation takes the states table as authoritative: any compaction (>=1) this session, or a banked state known stale vs live git HEAD, resolves to RECOVERY outright (outranking RED), not merely a floor -- because INV-3 says degraded in-context memory is not something a low context percentage should be able to mask. safeBoundary modulates advice text only ('rotate now' vs 'reach a safe boundary urgently' vs unknown), never the state itself, per section 4's explicit instruction.

tickets.title: Reorientation on /clear, canonical-location verification, and the wrong-worktree deny gate
tickets.note: 84/84 ticket tests, 223/223 suite. Proven on the REAL estate both ways: canonical worktree -> oriented (6,928 chars, under the 10,000 cap); primary checkout -> WRONG WORKTREE (8,214 chars) with the banner ABOVE the next action, and live Write plus git commit both denied while git status still ran. The brief and the PreToolUse gate share one comparison module, so the brief cannot say "aligned" while the gate denies. New decisions AD-18 (gate keys on cwd/repo-root/branch only; HEAD reported, never denies), AD-19 (unknown location + known canonical -> DENY; no programme or guard-throws -> ALLOW), AD-20 (Larry owns the whole git lifecycle), AD-21 (verbatim EnterWorktree recovery protocol, embedded in the refusal). Q-5 reconciled and X-2 settled. Two real defects caught by tests: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref is sticky (live HEAD would have been silently wrong), and one programme has many state-file copies across worktrees (counting files disarmed the guard). Known bound: from a wholly unrelated repository the guard cannot discover the estate - mitigated by --estate, closed properly by T-14.

tickets.title: Post-clear model selection gate — verify the selected model before releasing implementation
tickets.note: Closes the live defect: bank recommended Opus, session was visibly Auto, reorientation did not present the model recommendation before anything else, and implementation reconnaissance began before the model was verified. tools/governor/model-gate.mjs: pure core (resolveCurrentModel/evaluateModelGate/renderCompactGate/isAutoLabel/normaliseModelFamily) + one impure composition function (applyModelGate) + a CLI (`node model-gate.mjs check --state <path> --session <id>`) for the post-selection recheck. Composed additively onto reorient.mjs's runHook (3-line diff: one import, one wrapping call) WITHOUT modifying the pure reorient() function itself — reorient.test.mjs's existing 34/34 tests pass byte-for-byte unmodified, proven by git diff showing zero changes to that file. Verified structurally sound by an independent agent (not the original author) before landing: applyModelGate is a true no-op whenever the underlying reorient() result does not already permit implementation (covers WRONG_WORKTREE/FAILED/MISSING/CORRUPT/AMBIGUOUS/SKIPPED), and there is no circular import between model-gate.mjs and reorient.mjs. Fail-closed to UNKNOWN per requirement 6, recorded honestly as new fog (map F-9): the only real signal available (health-store model.id/display_name) reports the RESOLVED concrete model, not confirmed to distinguish "Auto resolved here" from "explicitly pinned" — a label containing "auto" is treated as a confirmed block; absence of any fresh session-matched sample is UNKNOWN, never a pass. 27/27 new tests (model-gate.test.mjs) covering AUTO, UNKNOWN (explicit INV-1 assertion), explicit MISMATCH/MATCH, stale-past and stale-future samples, cross-session samples, the exact 6-line compact format (regex-checked), the true no-op property, the AD-5 10,000-char cap under a synthetic oversized context (proves the ORIGINAL brief truncates, never the gate banner), distinct EXIT_CODEs per STATUS, and a full live acceptance test using REAL modules against a REAL scratch git estate and REAL health-store temp dir: bank -> blocked with no sample via the real runHook -> real writeHealthSample simulating model selection -> MATCH via the real CLI run as an actual subprocess (not an in-process call). Known, honestly-stated gap: T-03's sampler remains unwired from the live statusLine command (deliberately deferred at T-03, unchanged here), so the acceptance test writes the sample directly, mirroring T-12's synthetic-adapter precedent — this proves the gate mechanism, not full production wiring; wiring the sampler live remains a separate, not-yet-authorised step. 447/447 suite-wide, zero regressions.

locked_decisions.decision: statusLine is the primary telemetry source; the transcript is corroboration only, and must always be tail-read.
locked_decisions.why: statusLine is a documented, stable contract; the transcript format is explicitly internal and version-fragile, and several local transcripts are 30-40 MB.

locked_decisions.decision: Two separate stores: session health (ephemeral, machine-local) and programme state (durable, git-versioned).
locked_decisions.why: Different lifetimes and audiences. Conflating them is how banked state gets lost.

locked_decisions.decision: BLIND is a first-class state with its own exit code. Unreadable telemetry is never GREEN.
locked_decisions.why: INV-1, and the direct lesson of the 2026-07-29 controls that reported success over ground they never examined.

locked_decisions.decision: Compaction is counted by the PreCompact hook, never inferred from the transcript.
locked_decisions.why: A local probe found zero reliable transcript markers for compaction.

locked_decisions.decision: Reorientation rides SessionStart(source="clear") to additionalContext, capped at 10,000 characters, so the injected brief is a POINTER document and not the state itself.
locked_decisions.why: The cap makes a full state dump impossible.

locked_decisions.decision: The RED preflight block fails OPEN.
locked_decisions.why: INV-2. A governor that traps Warwick in his own session is a worse defect than one that misses a rotation.

locked_decisions.decision: The map lives in git as markdown, not in an issue tracker.
locked_decisions.why: Subagents get no MCP tools, so a tracker-hosted map is unreadable by the very workers who need it.

locked_decisions.decision: The evaluator core is pure: evaluate(signals) to verdict, with zero filesystem, git or myPKA knowledge. Adapters gather signals.
locked_decisions.why: Portability, and it makes the state space unit-testable without an estate.

locked_decisions.decision: The Governor DERIVES Team Knowledge/fusion-brief/session-handoff.md; it never invents a rival handoff file.
locked_decisions.why: That file already declares itself as consumed by the next Larry session. A parallel handoff would create two competing SSOTs — the exact defect this build exists to prevent.

locked_decisions.decision: /rotate-session inherits close-session steps 1-3 only. Steps 4-7 (Librarian pass, graduation, ClickUp mirror, self-improvement review) are end-of-programme and must never run on a rotation.
locked_decisions.why: INV-4. A rotation that costs what a close costs will not get used, and an unused governor is worse than none.

locked_decisions.decision: Durable programme state lives at <programme.home>/programme-state.json — with the programme, on the programme’s branch — and banked.head_sha records the head the state DESCRIBES, i.e. the parent of the commit that carries the state file.
locked_decisions.why: A file cannot contain its own commit’s SHA. State banked on a feature branch describes commits that exist only on that branch, so parking it on main would make it lie the moment the branch advanced. Consumers comparing against live HEAD must exclude the banking commit itself.

locked_decisions.decision: The programme-state collector (T-13) never performs a git fetch, so branches.behind is permanently unknown under it.
locked_decisions.why: A trustworthy behind-count needs fresh remote-tracking refs, and a collector must not have side effects on the repository it is reporting on. Matches this document's own pre-existing branches.behind unknown declaration from T-09.

locked_decisions.decision: T-13 collects repository, worktrees, branches and pull_requests only. workers is never scanned or synthesised by the collector.
locked_decisions.why: Which subagent was dispatched, for which ticket, with what expected output, is programme knowledge the dispatching session holds — not something git, worktree-recon or gh can answer. F-7 already establishes live-worker detection is best-effort; inventing worker entries from an OS process scan would manufacture false precision under a field whose entire schema purpose (T-09's D-2) is refusing to let a guessed collection read as ground truth.

locked_decisions.decision: THE ARTEFACT HIERARCHY (settled 2026-07-31, binding). (1) The Goal / Build Contract (01-GOAL-CONTRACT.md) is the PRODUCT SSOT — outcome, invariants, scope. (2) The Wayfinder map (02-MAP.md) is the LIVE EXECUTION / NAVIGATION SSOT — architecture, settled decisions, fog, frontier, write-back. (3) The Implementation Plan is the INITIAL ROUTE ONLY — context, never prescription, superseded by the map the moment execution diverges. (4) programme-state.json and Team Knowledge/fusion-brief/session-handoff.md are GENERATED PROJECTIONS — never hand-authored, never a rival source; a disagreement between a projection and its source is a defect in the projection. (5) Before merge, enduring BUILD-018 records GRADUATE into Builds/BUILD-018-session-governor/; evidence may remain under Deliverables/.
locked_decisions.why: Resolves the "which file wins" question that a rotation makes acute: a fresh Larry reads four artefacts and must know their rank without asking. Ranking product above execution stops the map quietly redefining the outcome; declaring the projections generated is what makes /rotate-session regenerating them safe rather than destructive; the graduation clause keeps the durable record with the build (the estate's own Builds/ convention) rather than stranding it in a working folder. Refines AD-9 (map-over-tickets) and generalises AD-12 (the handoff is derived, never invented).

locked_decisions.decision: The wrong-worktree gate keys on cwd, repository root and branch ONLY. HEAD is compared and REPORTED, but never denies.
locked_decisions.why: The moment a session makes its first legitimate commit, its HEAD diverges from banked.head_sha. A gate keyed on HEAD would block the session for having succeeded, and would be switched off within the hour. Location is a precondition; head movement is normal progress, and staleness already has its own channel (AD-14).

locked_decisions.decision: Two unknowns, two directions. (a) Cannot establish where we are while a canonical location IS known -> DENY (unknown is never aligned). (b) No active programme found at all, or the guard itself throws -> ALLOW.
locked_decisions.why: Failing closed everywhere would let one guard bug become a total work stoppage on a machine running 22 worktrees; failing open everywhere would make the gate decorative. The split puts the strictness exactly where a canonical location exists to be violated. Threat model is first-party mistakes, not a malicious operator. Both directions are proven by test - an untested fail-direction is an assumption, not a control.

locked_decisions.decision: Warwick never manages branches, worktrees, commits, pushes or PR creation. Larry owns the complete Git lifecycle. Warwick's standing gate is merge-to-main, plus decisions that are genuinely his.
locked_decisions.why: Recorded as a decision rather than left as a habit because the failure it prevents is silent: a Larry that asks Warwick to "just run git checkout" has converted an orchestration failure into Warwick's problem, and the ask looks helpful in the moment. Printed in every reorientation brief and every refusal, so a fresh session inherits it without being told.

locked_decisions.decision: The EnterWorktree recovery protocol. Larry initiates it. Under Remote Control the approval may appear ONLY in the local terminal, so Larry must IMMEDIATELY say, verbatim: "Approve the pending EnterWorktree request in the local Claude terminal", then wait. Larry must NOT spin silently, must NOT continue via absolute paths, and must NOT ask Warwick to run git commands.
locked_decisions.why: Learned live on 2026-07-31: a pending approval invisible to the remote side reads as the assistant hanging, and five minutes vanished. The protocol is embedded verbatim in the deny message and in the brief rather than only in the map, because at the moment it is needed nobody is reading the map - the refusal is the only thing on screen.
